[1, 5] The decline in exits was particularly pronounced, reaching one of the lowest points since the global financial crisis. [1] This slowdown was primarily attributed to challenging monetary conditions, including high interest rates and broader market uncertainty. [1] The lethargy also extended to the private equity middle market, which saw a six-year low in deal volume. [2] Globally, private equity investments in the first nine months of 2023 were down 44% year-over-year, with North America seeing a 49% drop in value. [3] The slowdown was more pronounced in the number of fund closings, which dropped by 43% year-over-year for the first three quarters, with 554 funds wrapping up. [3] In Q3 specifically, 160 funds closed, a 50% decrease compared to the previous year. [3] Despite the overall decline, Q3 saw a bump in capital raised to $153 billion, largely due to the closing of a few mega-funds, including vehicles from Clayton, Dubilier & Rice and Apollo. [1, 3] These large funds played a significant role in the fundraising landscape. [1] In contrast, mid-market funds, defined as those between $100 million and $5 billion, demonstrated resilience and even outperformed larger funds, accounting for 58.7% of funds by count year-to-date, their highest proportion since 2009. [1, 13] This outperformance was partly attributed to their ability to finance deals in a leverage-constrained environment. [1] <4> On September 20, 2023, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) adopted amendments to Rule 35d-1, the 'Names Rule,' under the Investment Company Act of 1940. [1, 2, 3] The SEC's orders found that by using their websites, the firms disseminated these advertisements to a mass audience. [1, 4] In addition to the Marketing Rule violations, two of the advisers were charged with failing to maintain required copies of their advertisements. [1, 3] Without admitting or denying the SEC's findings, the nine firms agreed to a censure, to cease and desist from further violations, and to pay combined penalties totaling $850,000. [3] The company's exchange-traded fund (ETF) platform was a significant driver of this growth, capturing the number one share of industry flows with $48 billion in net inflows for the quarter. In addition to strong investment performance, BlackRock's technology services revenue increased by 8% compared to the same period in the previous year, as client adoption of the Aladdin platform continued to show strong momentum. The official announcement and a corresponding teleconference for investors both occurred on July 14, 2023. [1, 4, 5] <8> T. Rowe Price, a U.S.-based global asset management firm, announced the appointment of Caroline Ramscar as its new environmental, social, and governance (ESG) investment specialist for the Asia Pacific (APAC) region. [1] Her role, which became effective on July 18, 2023, is based in Sydney. [1, 2, 3] Ramscar is responsible for engaging with clients across the APAC region on ESG matters and responsible investing strategies. [1, 3] She also supports the firm's suite of impact investment products, which span equities and fixed income. [2, 3] Ramscar has over 20 years of experience in financial markets and previously spent 10 years at Legal & General Investment Management in London, most recently as head of sustainability solutions. [3, 4] She reports to Nick Beecroft, the APAC Head of the Investment Specialist Group at T. Rowe Price. [2]

Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> On August 14, 2024, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) announced settled charges against 26 broker-dealers, investment advisers, and dually-registered firms for widespread and long-standing failures in maintaining and preserving electronic communications. The firms admitted to violating federal securities laws by failing to capture business-related communications on personal devices and unapproved messaging apps, often referred to as "off-channel communications." As a result, they agreed to pay combined civil penalties totaling $392.75 million. The penalties for individual firms ranged from $400,000 to $50 million. Notably, three firms that self-reported their violations received significantly lower penalties. In addition to the financial penalties, each firm was censured and ordered to cease and desist from future recordkeeping violations, and will engage independent compliance consultants to review their policies and procedures. <2> On July 19, 2024, the Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE) announced that five spot Ethereum Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) would begin trading on July 23, 2024, pending final regulatory effectiveness. The initial group of issuers confirmed for the launch on the CBOE included 21Shares (CETH), Fidelity (FETH), Franklin Templeton (EZET), Invesco Galaxy (QETH), and VanEck (ETHV). This move followed the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission's (SEC) approval of key 19b-4 filings in May 2024, with the final S-1 registration statements being the last step before trading could commence. In preparation for the launch, issuers disclosed their management fees, with many offering temporary waivers to attract early investment. <3> In its mid-July 2024 economic outlook, Vanguard stated that recent positive inflation data had raised the probability of an interest rate cut by the Federal Reserve. Vanguard's economists identified September as the most likely month for the first reduction. However, they noted this was conditional, stating that if shelter inflation remains excessively high, the Fed might not be in a position to cut rates at all in 2024. <4> In Bank of America's Global Fund Manager Survey conducted between July 5 and July 11, 2024, optimism regarding global economic growth declined significantly. The survey, which included 242 panelists managing $632 billion in assets, found that a net 27% of investors anticipate a weaker economy in the upcoming year, pushing economic sentiment down by 21 percentage points to a six-month low. This pessimism is largely influenced by a more negative outlook on U.S. growth, with a net 53% of investors—the highest number since December 2023—expecting the U.S. economy to weaken. Despite the grim growth forecast, a majority (68%) still believe a 'soft landing' is the most probable outcome for the global economy. For the first time in six months, high inflation was not the primary tail risk; instead, geopolitical conflict became the leading concern for investors. <5> The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) issued a proposed rule on July 3, 2024, aimed at strengthening and modernizing Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Countering the Financing of Terrorism (CFT) frameworks for financial institutions. [2] This proposal seeks to clarify and consolidate existing AML/CFT program requirements and would mandate that financial institutions implement an effective, risk-based program. [1] A key component of the proposed rule is the requirement for a formal risk assessment process to identify and mitigate illicit finance risks. [1] <6> BlackRock, the world's largest asset manager, announced an agreement on June 30, 2024, to acquire Preqin, a prominent provider of data and analytics for the alternative assets industry, for approximately $3.2 billion (£2.55 billion) in cash. [3, 5, 7, 9] The acquisition is a strategic move to significantly expand BlackRock's private markets data capabilities and integrate Preqin's extensive data and research tools with its Aladdin technology platform. [2, 3, 7, 12] This combination aims to provide clients with a unified platform for public and private market investments, complementing BlackRock's existing private markets solution, eFront. [5, 9] The deal is expected to capitalize on the rapid growth of the private markets sector. [2, 3] As part of the transaction, Preqin founder Mark O'Hare is set to join BlackRock as a Vice Chair. [5, 7] While Preqin's offerings will be integrated, it will also continue to be available as a standalone solution. [1, 4, 5] [1, 11] <7> On June 28, 2024, the U.S. Supreme Court issued a landmark 6-3 decision in *Loper Bright Enterprises v. Raimondo*, overturning the 'Chevron doctrine' that had been a core principle of administrative law for 40 years. [2, 10] This ruling eliminates the requirement for courts to defer to federal agencies' interpretations of laws that are ambiguous. [10] Writing for the majority, Chief Justice John Roberts stated that the Administrative Procedure Act (APA) requires courts to exercise their own "independent judgment" when determining if an agency has acted within its statutory authority. [5, 8] The decision came from a case brought by commercial fishermen who challenged a National Marine Fisheries Service rule requiring them to pay for the costs of federal observers on their vessels. [4, 6] While the ruling does not invalidate prior court decisions that relied on Chevron, it is expected to lead to increased legal challenges against new regulations from agencies like the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), fundamentally shifting the balance of power from regulatory bodies to the courts. [4, 9, 10] <8> On June 20, 2024, the Delaware General Assembly passed legislation amending the Delaware General Corporation Law (DGCL), which was then signed into law on July 17, 2024, and became effective on August 1, 2024. [2, 3] The amendments were enacted to codify prevailing market practices and abrogate recent Delaware Court of Chancery decisions, particularly *Moelis*, *Activision*, and *Crispo*, which some practitioners found inconsistent with those practices. [2, 5] Key changes include expressly authorizing corporations to enter into stockholder agreements that address corporate governance, such as granting consent rights over corporate actions. [2, 10] The legislation also clarifies rules for merger approvals, authorizing boards to approve agreements in "substantially final" form and confirming that associated disclosure schedules are not considered part of the merger agreement that requires board and stockholder approval. [2, 8] Additionally, the amendments permit merger agreements to include provisions for penalties and consequences for non-performance, such as reverse termination fees to cover stockholders' lost transaction premiums. [2, 6]

Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> US sustainable funds experienced net outflows of $5.7 billion in the second quarter of 2025, which concluded on June 30, 2025. This represented the 11th straight quarter of withdrawals, though the amount was a slight improvement over the $6.5 billion in outflows from the first quarter. According to a report published on July 25, 2025, the continued redemptions are partly explained by an anti-ESG backlash that has intensified under President Donald Trump’s administration. <2> Goldman Sachs Asset Management estimated that the aggregate funded status for U.S. corporate pension systems reached 104.4% at the close of the second quarter of 2025. This positive development was attributed to a rebound in U.S. equities, which was supported by resilient corporate earnings results in the first quarter. Other financial institutions also reported strong second-quarter results for corporate pension funds, citing the dual tailwinds of equity strength and stabilized liabilities. Milliman's Pension Funding Index noted a funded status of 104.9%, while MetLife Investment Management calculated an average funded ratio of 105.1%. These firms also identified strong stock market performance as the main driver for the growth. <3> A mid-year analysis of the US asset and wealth management sector for 2025 indicates a rebound in M&A dealmaking that began in late 2024 and continued into the first quarter of 2025. A key trend fueling this activity is the accelerated expansion of alternative and private market investment products into the retail channel, a strategic shift encouraged by the new US administration. However, the outlook is tempered by notable market volatility and uncertainty. Specific headwinds that could dampen future deal volume include tariff announcements made by U.S. President Donald Trump on April 2, 2025, alongside risks from increased labor costs, higher inflation, and rising interest rates. <4> In the second quarter of 2025, U.S. hedge funds marked their sixth straight month of net capital inflows, attracting an estimated $7.1 billion in June. [2] This contributed to a total inflow of $30 billion for the first half of the year. [2] Amid market uncertainties, a notable trend during this period was the adoption of barbell strategies, where funds invested in both high-growth technology stocks and defensive assets such as high-yield bonds. [1] This approach was a response to a market heavily concentrated in a few large tech stocks and facing macroeconomic risks. [1] <5> In a Q2 2025 report, Morningstar outlined key trends for the asset management sector in 2025, noting that market uncertainty stemming from fiscal, tariff, and monetary policies has heightened the volatility of asset manager stocks. [1] The report, titled '2025 Asset Management Trends to Know', also observed a significant focus on private credit fundraising among alternative asset managers, who have accounted for 90% of the capital raised in this area over the last five years. [1] Furthermore, Morningstar suggested that traditional asset managers are well-positioned to adopt artificial intelligence more rapidly due to their access to structured data. [1] <6> In a market analysis for July 2025, it was reported that U.S. equities, with technology companies at the forefront, surged to new highs fueled by strong earnings reports. Concurrently, economic data released on July 15, 2025, for the month of June showed a slight increase in inflation. The Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) saw a 0.3 percent rise on a seasonally adjusted basis. More specifically, the core CPI, which strips out volatile food and energy prices, registered a year-over-year increase of 2.9%. This uptick has led to the view that the Federal Reserve will likely maintain its 'wait-and-see' approach, thereby delaying any potential cuts to interest rates. <7> Brookfield Asset Management and Google announced a Hydro Framework Agreement for Google to procure up to 3,000 megawatts of carbon-free hydroelectric capacity in the U.S., marking the largest-ever corporate clean power deal for hydroelectricity. The first contracts executed under the agreement are 20-year Power Purchase Agreements for Brookfield's Holtwood and Safe Harbor hydroelectric facilities in Pennsylvania. These initial contracts are valued at over $3 billion and will supply 670 MW of capacity to support Google's operations in the PJM electricity market. In its Q2 2025 results for the quarter ending June 30, 2025, Brookfield also reported raising $22 billion in capital and announced the deployment of nearly $10 billion in infrastructure strategies. <8> The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) issued an administrative and cease-and-desist order against Suzanne Ballek, the former Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) of a registered investment adviser, on July 15, 2025. The settlement addresses actions that occurred between September 2022 and September 2023, when SEC examiners were conducting an examination of her employer, identified as Inland Investment Advisors LLC. In response to an SEC request, Ballek altered approximately 170 pre-clearance trading forms by modifying dates, filling in missing information, and, in some cases, creating new forms and affixing trader signatures without their knowledge. These actions were intended to create the false appearance that the forms were completed and signed correctly at the time of the transactions. Without admitting or denying the SEC's findings, Ballek consented to a cease-and-desist order, a civil penalty of $40,000, and a three-year ban from acting in a compliance capacity with any investment adviser or related entity. <9> On July 1, 2025, the SEC's Division of Corporation Finance issued guidance clarifying disclosure requirements for registration filings of crypto asset exchange-traded products (ETPs). [2, 3, 6] This guidance mandates that issuers provide detailed, plain-language information to protect investors and ensure market fairness. [7, 8] Key disclosure areas include the ETP's structure, such as its investment objectives, the plan of distribution, and the mechanics of creation and redemption. [1, 4] Issuers must also thoroughly outline the risks specific to the investment, including the volatility of the underlying crypto assets and potential for fraud or manipulation on trading platforms. [4, 7, 8] Furthermore, the guidance requires a comprehensive description of the underlying crypto assets, covering their origin, consensus mechanism, use cases, and total supply. [1, 7] Finally, detailed information regarding the custody of assets is required, specifying storage policies for private keys (e.g., cold or hot storage), whether assets are commingled, and the terms of custodial agreements. [4]

Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) announced on August 21, 2025, that Judge Margaret “Meg” Ryan has been appointed as the new Director of the Division of Enforcement. Her appointment is effective September 2, 2025. Judge Ryan succeeds Sam Waldon, who was serving as Acting Director and will resume his role as Chief Counsel for the Division. At the time of her appointment, Judge Ryan was a senior judge on the United States Court of Appeals for the Armed Forces. SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins stated that Judge Ryan "brings to the Commission decades of experience as a respected judge and practitioner of the law." <2> On August 15, 2025, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission's (SEC) Division of Investment Management issued new guidance, Accounting and Disclosure Information (ADI) 2025-16, for registered closed-end funds that invest in private funds (CE-FOPFs). This represents a major policy shift, reversing a 23-year-old informal staff practice. Under the new guidance, SEC staff will no longer request that these funds limit their investments in private funds to 15% of assets or restrict their offerings to accredited investors with a minimum investment of $25,000. This change effectively removes previous informal caps on exposure limits, investor eligibility, and minimum investments for CE-FOPFs, potentially increasing retail investor access to private fund strategies. <3> A market commentary published on August 6, 2025, highlighted a significant deceleration in the U.S. labor market. The analysis centered on the July jobs report, which indicated a payroll increase of only 73,000, prompting concerns about the durability of the economic recovery. This development was contextualized by the Federal Reserve's decision to maintain the federal funds rate at its meeting on July 29-30, 2025. <4> A report from Wolters Kluwer's Regulatory Violations Intelligence Index revealed an unprecedented decline in regulatory enforcement actions against U.S. financial services firms in the first half of 2025. Violation volumes fell by 37% compared to the last six months of 2024, with total monetary penalties dropping by 32%. The decline was observed across all tracked categories, with the most significant drop in competition-related offenses, where penalties decreased by 97%. This shift is attributed to a change in federal enforcement priorities, with some analysts noting that state-level enforcement is increasing to fill the void. <5> In July 2025, J.P. Morgan Asset Management reported that improved investor sentiment, driven by greater clarity on U.S. trade and fiscal policy, contributed to a 1.3% rise in global developed market equities. Key policy developments included the passage of the 'One Big Beautiful Bill Act' and new trade agreements with Japan and the European Union, which helped reduce the risk of an escalating trade war. Emerging market equities outperformed developed markets, rising 2.0%. The positive market performance was also supported by a strong second-quarter earnings season. As of August 1, 2025, with 66% of S&P 500 companies having reported, 82% had surpassed consensus earnings per share (EPS) estimates. This beat rate is significantly above the 5-year average of 78%. In aggregate, companies reported earnings that were 8.0% above estimates, leading to a blended earnings growth rate of 10.3% for the quarter, marking the third consecutive quarter of double-digit growth for the index. <6> Affiliated Managers Group (AMG) announced its financial results for the second quarter and first half of 2025 on July 31, 2025. The company reported a 15% year-over-year increase in Economic Earnings Per Share to $5.39. For the first half of 2025, AMG added approximately $55 billion in alternative assets under management, which included a record $33 billion in net inflows into alternatives. This brought the total alternative AUM to $331 billion. This growth was driven by over $8 billion in net client cash flows during the second quarter, marking the company's strongest organic growth in 12 years. Strategically, AMG announced four new partnerships in 2025 with firms that collectively manage about $24 billion in alternative strategies, including a new partnership with Montefiore Investment. Total assets under management reached $771 billion as of June 30, 2025. During the second quarter, the company repurchased approximately $100 million of its common stock. <7> A report from Wilshire published on July 31, 2025, indicates that the aggregate funded ratio for U.S. state pension plans rose by an estimated 3.4 percentage points during the second quarter of 2025, reaching 82.0%. This increase, which resulted in the strongest funded status since the end of 2021, was attributed to a 5.0% growth in asset value that counteracted a 0.7% rise in liability value. The improvement was largely driven by strong returns in the asset market, with the FT Wilshire 5000 Index achieving an all-time high during the quarter. <8> On or around July 29, 2025, a coalition of 26 Republican state finance officials from 21 states sent letters to 25 major U.S.-based asset management firms, including BlackRock, Vanguard, State Street, JPMorgan Chase, and Goldman Sachs. The officials urged the firms to prioritize their "traditional fiduciary duty" to clients over environmental, social, and governance (ESG) considerations.
